chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: Buying a Harry B. Jay cornet after Muggsy lent his
summary: The cornet he used for the Morton records was a Chicago-made Jay, bought after Muggsy Spanier left his horn at a 35th Street club.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Question I forgot to ask you a minute ago. You didn't remember the first horn you had. What make horn did you use about the time you were making those jelly roll records?

What make did you like? Oh, I think, uh, that was, uh, I believe I made, uh, made, uh, had a trumpet then of, uh, was made here in Chicago. Jay, Harry B. Jay. Oh, yeah. A cornet. I've heard, yeah, let's say Armstrong used one of those. Yes, yeah. It was a cornet. It was a cornet, yeah. I, I, uh, uh, the reason I bought that, uh, Jay, there was, uh, I was working with Jimmy Newton. I was working with Jimmy Newton on 35th Street at night, uh, after hour. Yeah. Nightclub. And, uh, Muggsy used to come in. Oh, yeah. Muggsy used to come in and sit in with him. Yeah. And he came in one night and, uh, I was telling him about my trumpet. I had a trumpet. It was going bad. Good stuff. Good stuff. Good stuff. Good stuff. Good stuff.

I was going to get a new trumpet and he mentioned about the J. He had one and so he left it there. He said, play that, you can play that tonight. He came in and left his horn there and he left, came back a little later. And so I blew that J and I liked it. So I went down that week I think and bought a J. And I kept that horn until I still have it. It's no good but it's still...
It was a cornet, not a trumpet. Cornet, yeah. You used that about that time.
